title: Justice4Nzoy – gemeinsam gegen Rassismus und Polizei!
content:
Samstag, 12. September 2026, 14 Uhr Landesmuseum Zürich: Justice4Nzoy! Demonstration gegen Rassismus, Polizeigewalt und die Aufrüstung der Herrschenden.


Roger Nzoy Wilhelm wurde am 30. August 2021 von einem Polizisten erschossen. Sein Tod ist kein Einzelfall. Bei Polizeieinsätzen allein im Kanton Waadt wurden in den letzten Jahren auch Lamin Fatty, Hervé Mandundu, Mike Ben Peter, Michael Kenechukwu Ekemezie, die 14-jährige Camila und der 17-jährige Marvin getötet.


Rassistische Polizeigewalt hat System: Sie beginnt bei den Polizeischikanen, denen People of Color täglich ausgesetzt sind, und endet immer wieder bei tödlicher Gewalt. Der Kampf für Gerechtigkeit für Nzoy ist deshalb auch ein Kampf gegen alle Formen des staatlichen Rassismus.


Die diesjährige Demonstration steht im Zeichen der Militarisierung. Rassistische Polizeigewalt und die aktuelle Aufrüstung der Herrschenden gehören zusammen. So beruht der Kapitalismus auf der Ausbeutung von Ressourcen und Arbeitskraft – hier und besonders gewaltsam im globalen Süden. Für diese Ausbeutung benötigt er rassistische Gewalt, die von kolonialer Dominanz über die globale Ausbeutung bis zum hochgerüsteten Migrationsregime reicht. Der Genozid in Palästina zeigt aktuell, welche Brutalität die imperialistische Dynamik des Kapitalismus entfesseln kann.


In Europa schreitet die Militarisierung voran. In der kapitalistischen Krise verschärfen sich die gesellschaftlichen Widersprüche und der Staat setzt zur Sicherung seiner Interessen vermehrt auf militärische Gewalt: Kriege gegen aussen und Repression gegen innen. Rassismus ist dabei ein wichtiges Machtmittel. Zur Klassengesellschaft gehören nicht nur die Widersprüche zwischen herrschender und arbeitender Klasse, sondern auch rassistische Spaltungen innerhalb der ausgebeuteten Klasse. People of Color werden systematisch in prekäre Arbeitsverhältnisse gedrängt. Antimuslimischer Rassismus normalisiert den Genozid in Gaza und die Repression gegen die Palästina-Solidarität. Polizeigewalt setzt die Klassenherrschaft durch und wird dabei von rassistischer Ideologie gestützt.


Doch dieser Unterdrückung steht eine reiche Geschichte des Widerstands entgegen. In Europa reicht sie von migrantischem Widerstand an den Grenzen und in den Knästen bis zu Kämpfen gegen Polizeibrutalität wie der Kampagne für Oury Jalloh. In den USA verbinden sich die Erfahrungen der Black Panthers, der Black-Lives-Matter-Bewegung und des Widerstands gegen ICE. In all diesen Kämpfen zeigt sich die zentrale Bedeutung der Community-Arbeit: der Organisierung in den Quartieren und dem Aufbau solidarischer Strukturen. Von diesen Erfahrungen können wir lernen. Das beste Mittel gegen rassistische Gewalt ist Klassenkampf – von unten nach oben! Die Kampagne Justice4Nzoy greift diese Praxis auf, wenn sie sich im Kreis 4 und darüber hinaus vernetzt.


Organisieren wir antirassistische Solidarität in den Quartieren und Betrieben! Wehren wir uns, wenn unsere Angehörigen, Nachbar:innen, Freund:innen und Arbeitskolleg:innen von Polizei und Migrationsämtern bedroht, erniedrigt und angegriffen werden!


Schaffen wir widerständige Quartiere!

author: Politisches Cafe in der K9
title: 50 Jahre Rock against Racism im Rückblick
content:
in der K9, Kinzigstraße 9 (Hinterhaus),


Berlin Friedrichshain, (Nähe U-Bahnhof Samariterstrasse)


Mittwoch, 16.09.2026, 19.30 Uhr


Runde Jahrestage werden ja eigentlich gern zur Identitätsvergewisserung genutzt. Etwas mag es da schon überraschen, dass es im Fall von 50 Jahre Punk, so der Eindruck nicht täuscht, doch eher ruhig geblieben ist. Sicher, auf arte und anderswo wird die für die Subkultur charakteristische rebellische Haltung abgefeiert und die üblichen Verdächtigen verlegen auf die musikalische Dimension fokussierte Erinnerungsliteratur. Blass bleiben hingegen die gesellschaftlichen Kontexte von Punk. Wir laden, mit dem bekannten Hintergrundbild des alten Clash-Promovideos zu ‚White Riot‘ aus dem Jahr 1976 im Hinterkopf, das randalierende Polizisten während des Notting Hill Carnivals im August 1976 zeigt, zu zwei kleinen Ausflügen in die ‚Kulissen‘.


Abend 1: White Riot? ‚Rock against Racism‘ im Rückblick


Who Shot the Sheriff? (Alan Miles, UK 2005, 66‘, OF)


Punk konstituierte sich im Moment einer tiefgreifenden Krise des fordistischen fixes in Großbritannien, in deren Rahmen erstmals in Europa, wenn wir von Italien mal absehen, rassistische und neofaschistische Kräfte wie die National Front bedrohlich an Raum in Politik, aber auch in Popular- und Jugendkultur zu gewinnen schienen. Hiergegen formierte sich ab Herbst 1976 von London ausgehend mit ‚Rock against Racism‘ eine Kampagne, die den Kampf auf dem Feld von Musik und (Jugend)Kultur selbst aufzunehmen trachtete und von Stuart Hall in seinem ersten Thatcherismus-Aufsatz „The Great Moving Right Show“ bereits 1979 als „one of the timeliest and best constructed of cultural interventions, repaying serious and extended analysis“ eingeschätzt wurde.


Alan Miles, im Hauptberuf bei der Londoner Feuerwehr beschäftigt, rekonstruierte die Geschichte der „Rock against Racism“- Kampagne der Jahre 1976/81 rückblickend im Moment ihrer Neuauflage unter dem Motto ‚Love Music Hate Racism‘ (2002) von ihrer Londoner Zentrale aus und mit Fokus auf die musikalische Dimension der Geschichte.


Zwar wurde die Kampagne in der BRD 1979/80 unter dem Motto ‚Rock gegen rechts‘ aufgegriffen, doch entwickelten sich diese Mobilisierungen in andere Richtungen; die wenigen deutschsprachigen Reflexionen zu RaR führen, von einem neueren Aufsatz von Gerd-Rainer Horn mal abgesehen, dementsprechend eher auf Abwege. Werfen wir also einen ersten Blick auf den Film (und vielleicht noch etwas Kleinkram) und schauen, was es mit RAR auf sich hatte, inwieweit die Geschichte noch relevant ist, was vielleicht davon gelernt werden könnte und ob es sich lohnen könnte, die Thematik zu einem späteren Zeitpunkt evt. noch einmal zu vertiefen.


(Beachtet bitte: Film in Englisch ohne Untertitel).

author: Ariana Figueroa
title: Appeals Court Blocks Trump Policy to Rapidly Deport Migrants to Third Countries
content:
The decision found that immigrants must have an opportunity to challenge their removal if they fear for their safety.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

A federal appeals court Friday struck down the Trump administration’s policy to quickly send noncitizens to countries they are not from, finding that immigrants must have an opportunity to challenge their removal if they fear for their safety.

The decision largely upheld a Boston federal judge’s February ruling that found the Department of Homeland Security’s policy unlawful. But the immigration officers can still conduct third-country removals if they follow the proper procedures, such as adequate notice and an opportunity for an immigrant to raise a fear-based claim to that country of removal.

Third-country removals, deportations from the United States to a nation other than an immigrant’s home country, occur when the immigrant’s home country does not accept the person’s repatriation.

Once rare, the procedure has spiked under the second Trump administration that has entered into partnerships with several countries, some with human rights concerns, to take third-country removals from the U.S.

The three-judge panel of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 1st Circuit also raised doubts that a country that accepts a person that is not their own citizen could “credibly provide blanket assurances that all removed noncitizens will not be persecuted or tortured there unless it intends to provide them with some sort of affirmative protection against rogue agents and non-state actors.”

The panel also upheld the lower court’s finding that the notice to a third country was inadequate — about 24 hours — and that the policy was unlawful.

It gives “no notice at all of an impending third-country removal when the country to which the noncitizen is to be removed has provided credible (in the State Department’s judgment) diplomatic assurances that noncitizens removed there from the United States will not be persecuted or tortured,” the panel wrote.

The panel included circuit judges Lara E. Montecalvo, Jeffrey R. Howard and Seth R. Aframe. Former President Joe Biden nominated Montecalvo and Aframe. Former President George W. Bush nominated Howard.

The Trump administration in May 2025 made an emergency request to the Supreme Court after U.S. District Judge Brian Murphy blocked the policy. The Supreme Court in June 2025 temporarily allowed for the removals, before sending it back to the lower court.

Murphy again in February issued an order that blocked the policy and required DHS to carry out the statutory obligations of proper notice of removal to a third country and to give a noncitizen enough time to raise any concerns for their safety to their removal to a third country.

The Trump administration later appealed to the First Circuit, and could appeal again to the Supreme Court.

DHS did not respond to States Newsroom’s request for comment Friday.

author: Giulia Messmer
title: Sea-Watch gewinnt vor Gericht: Festsetzung der Sea-Watch 5 in Neapel aufgehoben
content:
Neapel, Italien: Das Gericht in Neapel hat die 45-tägige Festsetzung der Sea-Watch 5 und das Bußgeld in Höhe von 7.500 Euro aufgehoben. Die Sanktionen waren mit dem Vorwurf verhängt worden, Sea-Watch habe während eines Rettungseinsatzes im August nicht mit den libyschen Behörden kommuniziert. Sea-Watch hält das Vorgehen für unrechtmäßig und legte dagegen Klage ein. In einer vorläufigen Entscheidung folgte das Gericht der Argumentation von Sea-Watch und hob sowohl die Festsetzung als auch das Bußgeld auf. Die Sea-Watch 5 kann nun wieder auslaufen, um Rettungseinsätze durchzuführen.

Die Sanktionen gegen Sea-Watch wurden verhängt im Anschluss an einen Rettungseinsatz am 13. August, bei dem die Crew der Sea-Watch 5 sechs Menschen in internationalen Gewässern aus dem Wasser rettete. Nachdem die italienischen Behörden das Schiff angewiesen hatten, den weit entfernten Hafen von Neapel anzulaufen, wurde der Crew bei ihrer Ankunft vorgeworfen, die libyschen Behörden nicht über die Rettung informiert zu haben. Daraufhin wurde das Schiff festgesetzt.

Sea-Watch begrüßt die Entscheidung des Gerichts als jüngsten Erfolg in einer Reihe erfolgreicher rechtlicher Schritte gegen Blockaden ziviler Seenotrettungsschiffe auf Grundlage des sogenannten Piantedosi-Dekrets. Dieses verpflichtet Rettungscrews, den Anweisungen der italienischen Behörden Folge zu leisten, während Rettungseinsätzen mit der sogenannten libyschen Küstenwache zu kommunizieren. Sea-Watch ist Teil der Justice Fleet, eines Bündnisses ziviler Seenotrettungsorganisationen, das die Zusammenarbeit mit libyschen Akteuren, die in schwere Menschenrechtsverletzungen involviert sind, kategorisch ablehnt.

Sea-Watch-Sprecherin Julia Winkler erklärt:

„Diese Entscheidung bringt ein Gesetz ins Wanken, das von Anfang an illegitim war. Libyen ist kein sicherer Ort. Die sogenannte libysche Küstenwache ist Teil der Gewalt, vor der Menschen fliehen – und kein legitimer Akteur der Seenotrettung. Die Zusammenarbeit der EU mit Libyen zur Externalisierung von Migrationsabwehr ist ein Verbrechen gegen die Menschenrechte. Punkt.“

Juristische Erfolge können verlorene Rettungszeit nicht zurückbringen. Seit 2023 haben die italienischen Behörden zivile Rettungsschiffe mehr als 40 Mal festgesetzt und ihnen damit insgesamt mehr als 900 Einsatztage genommen. Die Festsetzung der Sea-Watch 5 war allein im Jahr 2026 bereits die achte derartige Maßnahme. Bis Mitte September waren zivile Rettungsschiffe in diesem Jahr bereits mehr als 200 Tage lang daran gehindert worden, Einsätze durchzuführen.

Das sind Tage, an denen Rettungsschiffe gezwungen waren, im Hafen zu bleiben, während weiterhin Menschen auf See starben: Im Jahr 2026 sind auf den Fluchtrouten über das Mittelmeer bereits mehr als 1.700 Menschen gestorben oder werden vermisst. Seit Giorgia Meloni im Amt ist, haben mehr als 10.000 Menschen im Mittelmeer ihr Leben verloren.

author: By Sean Summers, Unicorn Riot
title: Three Arrested and Charged for Disrupting Border Wall Construction
content:
Cochise County, AZ — On Monday a set of arrests stemming from the ongoing U.S.-Mexico border wall blockade in southeastern Arizona saw three protesters jailed overnight. The arrests mark the first charges in the now

months-long struggle against construction

 of a double border wall along the international border in Arizona.


Three protesters were arrested by the Cochise County Sheriff’s Office and booked on charges of disorderly conduct, according to a source on the ground and a press release from local law enforcement.


Video posted to Instagram showed protesters dressed as birds and jaguars, both of which live in the area and rely on the borderlands as their habitat, walking around a worksite along the border wall’s construction zone.


via rally.forthevalley on Instagram


Alex Chabbott, one of the protesters who was arrested Monday, told Unicorn Riot the demonstration was light-hearted and calm, centering around costumed land defenders mimicking local wildlife. Chabbot said four people — two dressed as birds, two as jaguars — paraded around the worksite and interrupted concrete pouring and gravel transportation.


But shortly after they arrived, a construction foreman at the work site parked vehicles around the pickup truck protesters drove there in, Chabbott said, boxing them in. Unable to leave, the group of six people who had traveled there in the truck stayed on the scene.


While boxed in, they said, a foreman tried to enter the truck to take pictures. Chabbott told Unicorn Riot that the foreman threatened and shoved one protester during the attempt to photograph the truck.


After protesters had disrupted work for about an hour, Sheriff’s deputies responded and detained them. A

press release

 from the Cochise County Sheriff’s Office accuses the protesters of trespassing in a “restricted construction area.” Three were ultimately arrested and booked into the Cochise County jail in Bisbee, Arizona.


Police and Customs and Border Patrol responded, Chabbott said, before the three were transported to the county jail by the Cochise County Sheriff’s Office.


While most of the ongoing border wall blockade activity has taken place in Santa Cruz County, Monday’s action and resulting arrests happened in neighboring Cochise County.


The Sheriff of Santa Cruz County, David Hathaway, has voiced his

opposition

 to the border wall’s construction and has reportedly refused to charge or arrest protesters involved in the now months-long blockade opposing the wall in that county.


Cochise County Sheriff Mark Dannels, on the other hand, has long

peddled inaccurate claims about border security

 and more recently has become a recurring character in MAGA social and political circles.


As the

Phoenix New Times

 documented, Dannels received a $1 million grant from the Department of Homeland Security shortly after agreeing to collaborate with ICE under a

287(g) agreement

, $250,000 of which is earmarked specifically to fund Dannels traveling to border policy conferences and other functions.


Dannels regularly tours with politicians along the section of border wall that crosses his jurisdiction, and in 2025 he was appointed to President Trump’s Homeland Security Advisory Committee.


The three protesters had an initial appearance in Bisbee Justice Court Tuesday morning. Each were released on personal recognizance orders with no bail, but with instructions to avoid the worksite they were arrested at and contact with the workers they encountered there, Chabbott said. Judge Janus Poppe entered a not guilty plea for all three defendants. A

support fund

 for legal defense of the three defendants has been created.

author: Joe Sandler Clarke
title: UK Lawyers for Israel Want Doctors Without Borders Branded a Terror Group
content:
A group of pro-Israel lawyers is urging the UK government to label Doctors Without Borders a terrorist organisation over its work in Gaza. 


UK Lawyers for Israel (UKLFI) allege that the charity – which provides life-saving medical aid to people in warzones – has links to militant groups, and have called on home secretary Shabana Mahmood to proscribe the charity.


If acted on, the move would see the Nobel Peace prize-winning NGO – also known as Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) – categorised the same way as Isis in UK law. It would also make donating to or expressing support for the group a criminal offence. 


Throughout its genocide in Gaza, Israel’s military has

killed 15 MSF employees

, as well as over 1,000 other humanitarian workers,

according to the UN

. 


On Monday, MSF said Israel had bombed one of its buses, injuring one of 10 humanitarian workers on board. The bus was clearly marked as an MSF vehicle, the charity said in a statement. 


“Once again, Israeli forces have shown a blatant disregard for the safety of humanitarian and medical personnel. Nowhere is safe in Gaza. Civilians, healthcare workers and humanitarian staff must be protected,” it added.


UKLFI allege links between people working for MSF in Palestine and militant organisations. 


In a report shared with the home secretary, they note the example of Fadi Al-Wadiya, who worked as a physiotherapist with MSF and was killed in an airstrike by Israeli forces on Gaza City on 25 June 2024. In February 2026, the militant group Palestine Islamic Jihad stated that Al-Wadiya had been a member of the group. 


MSF has denied any links to militant organisations in Palestine and said it had no knowledge of Al-Wadiya participating in military activity. It added that Israeli authorities never provided accurate information to the NGO about his alleged involvement. 


The Israeli government has repeatedly claimed MSF has links with militant groups in Palestine and has looked to restrict the charity’s work within the occupied Palestinian territories, including by limiting imports of medicine and other supplies. 


Earlier this year, Israel expelled MSF’s international staff from Gaza, along with people from other NGOs, saying they had failed to provide a list of names of individuals working for the charity. 


In a piece published on

MSF’s website

 in March, Rocío Simón Martínez, a nursing manager with MSF in Gaza, said the move to expel international staff “will have catastrophic consequences for people who depend almost entirely on humanitarian assistance”.

author: infolibre
title: Με την αμερικανική ριζοσπαστική αριστερά ενάντια στην τεχνητή νοημοσύνη και την κλιματική καταστροφή!
content:
Του Γιώργου Μητραλιά


Το γεγονός ότι υπάρχει μια εξαίρεση στην παγκόσμια ραγδαία άνοδο της ακροδεξιάς και ότι αυτή η εξαίρεση παίρνει σάρκα και οστά στην καρδιά του παγκόσμιου καπιταλισμού, στις Ηνωμένες Πολιτείες της Αμερικής, δεν μπορεί παρά να αφήσει εντελώς έκπληκτους και άναυδους όλους εκείνους που μεγάλωσαν με τη βεβαιότητα ότι τίποτα δεν μπορεί να αλλάξει στην βαθιά αντιδραστική κοινωνία της αμερικανικής υπερδύναμης. Γι’ αυτό άλλωστε, όπως και σχεδόν παντού αλλού, στη χώρα μου, την Ελλάδα, το προσφιλές σύνθημα ολόκληρης της αριστεράς που φωνάζεται στις διαδηλώσεις εδώ και μισό αιώνα. είναι το πολύ εύγλωττο και κάπως απλοϊκό, αν όχι ρατσιστικό… «

Αμερικανοί φονιάδες των λαών»…


Έτσι, ενώ παντού αλλού, και κυρίως στην Ευρώπη, αυτή η ραγδαία άνοδος της ακροδεξιάς οδηγεί σε ιστορικές εκλογικές επιτυχίες και φοβίζει για ακόμα χειρότερα στους προσεχείς μήνες στη Γαλλία, την Ισπανία, το Ηνωμένο Βασίλειο και αλλού,

στις Ηνωμένες Πολιτείες διαπιστώνεται ένα διαμετρικά αντίθετο φαινόμενο

: από τη μια, η άλλοτε θριαμβεύουσα αμερικανική ακροδεξιά, που ενσαρκώνει ο ίδιος ο πρόεδρος Τραμπ, βρίσκεται σε μια ολοένα και βαθύτερη κρίση, καθώς απορρίπτεται από τη μεγάλη πλειοψηφία ενός απογοητευμένου και οργισμένου αμερικανικού πληθυσμού. Και από την άλλη, αυτή η κρίση της αμερικανικής ακροδεξιάς συμβαδίζει με την

εκρηκτική άνοδο της νέας ριζοσπαστικής αριστεράς

, που σημειώνει διαδοχικές εκλογικές επιτυχίες και βλέπει την επιρροή της να αυξάνεται σε χρόνο ρεκόρ! (1)


Είναι προφανές ότι τέτοια γεγονότα ιστορικής εμβέλειας, που εκτυλίσσονται στην ίδια την καρδιά του παγκόσμιου καπιταλισμού, θα επηρεάσουν πολύ πέρα από τα σύνορα των Ηνωμένων Πολιτειών. Και αυτό καθώς μάλιστα η αμερικανική ακροδεξιά δεν είναι μια οποιαδήποτε ακροδεξιά. Με την εξαιρετικά ενεργή υποστήριξη του ενοίκου του Λευκού Οίκου και της κυβέρνησής του, και έχοντας, κατά συνέπεια, στη διάθεση της τεράστια μέσα, η αμερικανική ακροδεξιά ενέπνευσε, υποστήριξε, χρηματοδότησε, εκπαίδευσε και κατεύθυνε, στα τελευταία δέκα χρόνια, τα κόμματα και τις οργανώσεις της ακροδεξιάς σε όλο τον κόσμο, με ιδιαίτερη προτίμηση στα πιο σκληροπυρηνικά, συμπεριλαμβανομένων των νεοφασιστικών και νεοναζιστικών σχηματισμών. Αυτό την έχει καταστήσει το κέντρο της «Φαιάς Διεθνούς» της εποχής μας, της οποίας εξάλλου ηγείται σε συνεργασία με τη Ρωσία του Πούτιν.


Το δίδαγμα που προκύπτει από τα παραπάνω βγάζει μάτια: το ειδικό βάρος και η καθοριστική σημασία της αμερικανικής ακροδεξιάς εντός της παγκόσμιας ακροδεξιάς έχουν για αποτέλεσμα ότι η βαθιά παρούσα κρίση της προκαλεί ή πρόκειται να προκαλέσει σύγχυση και απογοήτευση στις τάξεις της παγκόσμιας ακροδεξιάς, σηματοδοτώντας την παύση ή ακόμη και το τέλος της αδιάκοπης ραγδαίας ανόδου της τα τελευταία τουλάχιστον δέκα χρόνια. Ωστόσο, προσοχή: αυτή η κρίση δεν πέφτει από τον ουρανό, αλλά είναι, σε μεγάλο βαθμό, αποτέλεσμα της παρούσας ιστορικής ανόδου της αμερικανικής ριζοσπαστικής αριστεράς. Μιας ανόδου της ριζοσπαστικής Αριστεράς που επιδεινώνει πaραπέρα την κρίση της τραμπιστικής ακροδεξιάς, καθιστώντας την όλο και πιο αδιέξοδη, καθώς μάλιστα αυτή η άνοδος επιτυγχάνεται σε βάρος και του κατεστημένου του Δημοκρατικού Κόμματος, και άρα σε βάρος του παραδοσιακού δικομματισμού και του (καπιταλιστικού) συστήματος που το δημιούργησε και το συντηρεί!


Το δίδαγμα που πρέπει να αντλήσει η ευρωπαϊκή Αριστερά είναι όχι μόνο ότι έχει πολλά να μάθει από τις εμπειρίες της αμερικανικής ριζοσπαστικής Αριστεράς, αλλά και, κυρίως, ότι πρέπει να συμμαχήσει και να συντονιστεί μαζί της το συντομότερο δυνατό!

 Και αυτό ανεξάρτητα από τις διαφορές ή ακόμα και τις διαφωνίες που μπορεί να υπάρχουν στο άλφα ή στο δείνα ζήτημα. Επειδή η ενότητα δράσης επιβάλλεται σε όλους και όλες μας περισσότερο από ποτέ, σε μια δραματική στιγμή της ιστορίας της ανθρωπότητας κατά την οποία ο συντονισμός των δυνάμεών μας συνιστά μια απεγνωσμένη κατεπείγουσα υποχρέωση.…


Και όταν κάνουμε λόγο για απεγνωσμένη κατεπείγουσα υποχρέωση, δεν πρόκειται διόλου ούτε για υπερβολή ούτε για ρητορικό σχήμα. Ήταν ήδη απεγνωσμένα κατεπείγουσα υποχρέωση εξαιτίας της κλιματικής καταστροφής που επιταχύνεται και δείχνει πλέον να φτάνει σε σημεία καμπής με συνέπειες που μοιάζουν πια με εφιάλτη. Όμως, η υποχρέωση γίνεται ακόμη πιο επείγουσα από τότε που ερευνητές στον τομέα της Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης προειδοποιούν δημοσίως ότι η ΤΝ απειλεί άμεσα την ίδια την επιβίωση της ανθρωπότητας (!), και διευθύνοντες σύμβουλοι γιγάντων της ΤΝ, όπως η Anthropic και η OpenAI, υπαινίσσονται, επίσης …

author: Publicación Abierta
title: La filosofía de la liberación: ¿continuidad del marxismo o del peronismo? Una genealogía reprimida
content:
Introducción: una pregunta que nunca se formuló en serio


Junio de 1971, Alta Gracia, provincia de Córdoba, Argentina. Allí se celebra el II Congreso Nacional de Filosofía, donde un grupo que luego sería conocido como “filosofía de la liberación” se presenta por primera vez de manera colectiva. El lugar está a pocos kilómetros de la ciudad de Córdoba, donde dos años antes había estallado el Cordobazo: una insurrección obrera y estudiantil que conmovió los cimientos de la dictadura de Onganía y que fue vivida por sus protagonistas como una batalla contra un Estado servil a los intereses del capital transnacional.


Dos años separan ambos acontecimientos. En el mismo suelo, se suceden dos formas de “liberación”: primero la práctica, obrera, estudiantil, callejera, antimperialista; después la teórica, académica, filosófica, organizada en torno a las categorías de “exterioridad” y “otro”. Esta superposición geográfica y temporal, si se explica solamente por la “coincidencia”, resulta cuando menos sospechosa.


La tesis de este artículo es la siguiente: la filosofía de la liberación, en su origen, es el eco diferido de la gramática política de la Tercera Posición peronista en el campo de la filosofía, y no la prolongación natural del linaje marxista. Su posterior narración como “marxismo latinoamericano” es, en buena medida, una reconstrucción genealógica operada después del exilio, orientada a obtener legitimidad académica. El costo de esa reconstrucción fue la pérdida del filo tercerista que la hacía incómoda tanto al capitalismo como al marxismo ortodoxo.


 El “pueblo” peronista y la apropiación categorial de la filosofía de la liberación


Para comprender el origen de la filosofía de la liberación hay que comprender primero la operación central del peronismo filosófico. El 9 de abril de 1949, Perón pronunció ante el Primer Congreso Nacional de Filosofía el discurso que luego circularía como La comunidad organizada. Allí definió una “tercera vía” que no era ni el individualismo capitalista ni el colectivismo comunista. Los estudios sobre este texto señalan que la “comunidad organizada” constituye “la base filosófica, política y social del justicialismo como tercera posición frente al individualismo capitalista y el colectivismo comunista”.


El núcleo de esa “tercera posición” es la redefinición del sujeto histórico. Un texto doctrinal peronista lo formula sin ambigüedad: “Para el marxismo, el sujeto de la historia es ‘la clase’… Para la Tercera Posición, en cambio, el sujeto de la historia es ‘el pueblo'”. Esa sustitución —”pueblo” en lugar de “clase”— es lo que distingue al peronismo del marxismo, no una variante interna del mismo.


Ahora bien, ¿qué hizo la filosofía de la liberación con esa categoría? El análisis clásico de Horacio Cerutti Guldberg sobre las diferencias internas de la filosofía de la liberación es concluyente. El “sector populista” —Dussel, Scannone, Ardiles— opera exactamente con la misma sustitución: “ya no se habla de individuo (capitalismo) ni de clase (marxismo), se habla de pueblo”. Y ese sector “reelabora ciertos aspectos de la doctrina peronista (tercera vía o posición)”. La conclusión de Cerutti no admite rodeos: la categoría central de la filosofía de la liberación, “pueblo”, proviene del peronismo, no del marxismo.


Cerutti ubica a Dussel en el “populismo de la ambigüedad abstracta”, cuyo rasgo es “una opción fidelista, de fe religiosa, anterior al filosofar” y “una visión hegeliana de la historia de la filosofía”. Es decir: el punto de partida de Dussel no es la lectura de Marx, sino una opción político-religiosa previa.


 


 Kusch: el caso que no se puede eludir


Si el análisis categorial se mantuviera en el plano de los textos, el caso de Rodolfo Kusch ofrece una evidencia biográfica directa.


La investigación de Marcin Forcini confirma que Kusch fue miembro institucional del grupo de filosofía de la liberación entre 1971 y 1975: “participaba de las reuniones, colaboraba en las publicaciones, ocupaba cargos institucionales”. Al mismo tiempo, “coordinó el Frente Peronista de Liberación Cultural ‘Hugo Arrieta’, cuyas actividades se desarrollaron entre 1973 y 1974”.


El análisis de Forcini sobre El pensamiento indígena y popular en América (1973) es aún más preciso: ese texto “constituye una toma de posición política” y su postura “se inscribe en el campo de la derecha peronista”, continuando “una larga tradición de denuncia de la ‘infiltración marxista'” en el peronismo. Ambos …

title: Borsadaki fon çöküşü Meclis gündeminde: Bayhan’dan Bakan Şimşek'e istifa çağrısı
content:
Duygu Ayber Gültekin [email protected]

Borsa İstanbul'da 7 portföy yönetim şirketine ait 130 yatırım fonunun tasfiye edilmesiyle sonuçlanan milyarlarca liralık temerrüt krizi, Türkiye Büyük Millet Meclisi (TBMM) gündemine taşındı. Emek Partisi (EMEP) İstanbul Milletvekili İskender Bayhan, Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı Mehmet Şimşek’in yanıtlaması istemiyle verdiği soru önergesinde, krizin maliyetinin kamu kaynaklarıyla üstlenilmesini sert bir dille eleştirdi. "Özel finansal varlıkların değerlenmesinden doğan olağanüstü kârlar sermaye çevrelerine kalırken kriz döneminde kamu likiditesi ve kamu sermayeli kuruluşların devreye girmesi, faturanın emekçi halka kesilmesi anlamına gelmektedir" diyen Bayhan, Bakan Şimşek'i siyasi sorumluluk üstlenerek istifa etmeye çağırdı.

TBMM Başkanlığı'na sunulan önergede, krizin göz göre göre geldiğine dikkat çekildi. Bakan Şimşek’in 4 Kasım 2025 tarihinde yaptığı "bazı fonlar üzerinden manipülasyonların yapıldığını biliyoruz" ve "düzenleme eksikliği var" şeklindeki açıklamalarını hatırlatan Bayhan, ekonomi yönetiminin sürece seyirci kaldığını savundu. Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu'nun (SPK) olağandışı fon hareketlerini 2025'in son çeyreğinde tespit ettiğini ve konunun 2 Aralık 2025'te bizzat Şimşek'in başkanlığındaki Finansal İstikrar Komitesi'nde ele alındığını belirten Bayhan, “Riskleri bildiğiniz halde bunların yaklaşık 1 yıl boyunca büyümeye devam etmesinin siyasi ve idari sorumluluğu kime aittir?” diyerek Şimşek'ten açıklama talep etti. Borsa İstanbul, SPK ve Takasbank'ın piyasa gözetim mekanizmalarının bilerek işletilmediğini vurgulayan Bayhan, riskler sistemik hale geldikten sonra alınan kapatma ve tasfiye kararlarının idari sorumlularının hesap vermesi çağrısında bulundu.

Hükümetin ekonomi politikalarının işçi ve emekçileri finansal sisteme mahkûm ettiğini belirten Bayhan, 2003'te başlayan Bireysel Emeklilik Sistemi (BES) ve 2017'de devreye sokulan Otomatik Katılım Sistemi'nin (OKS) son OVP hedefleri doğrultusunda daha da genişletildiğine dikkat çekti. TCMB'nin 10 Eylül 2026'da politika faizini yüzde 37'de tutarak uyguladığı para politikasının iç talebi ve ücretleri baskıladığını belirten Bayhan, dar gelirli yurttaşların konut veya otomobil sahibi olma vaadiyle tasarruf finansmanı şirketlerine mecbur bırakıldığını dile getirdi. "Yoksulluk sınırı altındaki ücretler ile ev, otomobil veya geleceğe yönelik birikim yapması olanaksız olan işçi ve emekçilerin cebindeki son kuruş dahi finansal araçlarınıza bağlanmıştır" diyen Bayhan, yurttaşları finansal piyasalardaki getiriye ve manipülasyonlara bağımlı hale getiren bu ekonomi politikalarına derhal son verilmesi çağrısında bulundu.

Fon krizinin ardından Merkez Bankası'nın piyasaya sağlayacağı likiditeyi artırması ve kamu sermayeli Emlak Katılım'ın Katılımevim ile Birevim'i satın almak üzere harekete geçmesi de Şimşek’e soruldu. Sermaye gruplarının borç, zarar veya yükümlülüklerinin bu yolla kamu bilançosuna aktarılıp aktarılmayacağını soran Bayhan, "Finansal varlıkların yükseldiği dönemde kazançların sermayeye bırakılıp, kriz çıktığında Merkez Bankası ve kamu kurumlarının devreye girmesi 'kazanç özel, zarar kamusal' bir ekonomi modelinin sonucu değil midir?" sorusunu yönelterek iktidarın kriz yönetimi anlayışını eleştirdi. 2027-2029 Orta Vadeli Program (OVP) kapsamındaki mali disiplin hedeflerine de atıf yapan Bayhan, "Bu krizin doğuracağı herhangi bir kamu maliyetinin işçi ve emekçilere daha yüksek vergiler, düşük ücret ve emekli aylığı artışları veya sosyal harcamaların kısılması yoluyla ödetilmeyeceğini taahhüt ediyor musunuz?" dedi.

Gelinen noktada Tera, Pusula, Hedef, Atlas, A1, Pardus ve Bulls Portföy'e ait 130 fonun işleminin durdurulması ve tasfiye edilmesi kararına değinen Bayhan, bu sürecin hangi nesnel kriterlere göre yürütüldüğünün kamuoyuna açıklanmasını istedi. Tasfiye kapsamına alınan bazı grupların herhangi bir likidite veya temerrüt sorunu yaşamadıklarını iddia ettiklerine işaret eden Bayhan, "Hangi fonların tasfiye edileceği, hangilerinin yeniden faaliyete geçirileceği ve bu yeniden yapılanmanın maliyetini nihai olarak kimin üstleneceği açıklanmalıdır" diyerek yetkililere seslendi. Krize göz yumulduğunu ve müdahalede kasıtlı olarak geç kalındığını bir kez daha yineleyen Bayhan, "Manipülasyonu önceden bildiğiniz, konunun sizin başkanlığınızdaki Finansal İstikrar Komitesinde görüşüldüğü halde bugün gelinen tablo karşısında Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı olarak siyasi sorumluluk üstlenmeyi ve görevden istifa etmeyi düşünüyor …

author: Unknown
title: How to Understand Key Terms in Large Language Models
content:
When you use AI to write, read reports, or work with files, you may encounter terms such as

token

,

context

, and

agent

. These terms help explain what happens when you give an AI application a task: what information it can use, how it produces a response, and whether it can take actions such as searching for sources or saving a document.


This guide introduces the main terms related to

large language models (LLMs)

 through practical examples. It begins with how models process information, then explains how to give them instructions and reference material, how tools and agents carry out tasks, and how to organise ongoing work. It also introduces ways to access models through other software or run them on your own equipment.


1.  How Language Models Work


Large Language Models


A

large language model (LLM)

 is an AI model trained on vast amounts of text and other data to learn patterns in language. ‘Large’ refers to its scale, including the number of internal parameters adjusted during training.


When generating text, a typical LLM uses the information available to it – including your instructions and the text already written – to predict what could come next. More precisely, it predicts the next

token

, a small unit of text such as a word or part of a word. It selects a token, adds it to the text, and repeats the process. In this way, it builds a response step by step.


Many people first encounter LLMs through a question-and-answer conversation. But the same process also allows models to summarise documents, translate, and draft text. A fluent response, however, is not necessarily a correct one: generating plausible language does not guarantee factual accuracy.


Token


A

token

 is a small unit of text that a language model processes. Before your message reaches the model, a tool called a

tokeniser

 splits it into tokens. A token may be a whole word, part of a word, or a punctuation mark. Spaces can also form part of a token.


For example, a tokeniser might keep ‘cat’ as one token but split ‘playing’ into ‘play’ and ‘ing’. This is an illustration, not a fixed rule: different tokenisers can split the same text differently. A token is therefore not the same thing as a word, and counting words will not give you an exact token count.


Each token is assigned a numerical ID so that the model can process the text as numbers. When generating a reply, the model predicts tokens one at a time. These tokens are then converted back into the text you see on screen.


Token counts matter when using a model.

Input tokens

 are the tokens in the material supplied to it, such as your instructions, documents, and any earlier messages included in the conversation.

Output tokens

 are the tokens it generates. Many model providers charge for API use based on these counts, often at different rates for input and output. Models also have limits on how many tokens they can process or generate in one request.


Longer texts generally require more tokens. The language also makes a difference: expressing the same meaning in different languages can produce different token counts. To find the exact count for a piece of text, you need the tokeniser used by that model.


Pre-trained Knowledge


Token prediction explains how a model produces text, but it does not yet explain why a model can answer questions without being given any external files. The answer lies in what it learnt during training. During training, a large language model learns patterns and information from massive amounts of text, code, and other data.


This is also why, even if we do not provide the model with any external files, it can still answer a large number of questions about common sense, history, maths, programming, and so on. This content is not obtained by the model through temporary searching. The model has already learnt patterns related to this information during training. This information is often described as the model’s

pre-trained knowledge

.


However, the model does not have a perfect database of facts. It learns patterns from its training data, and these patterns can sometimes be incomplete, outdated,

biased

, or simply wrong. When the model does not have enough reliable information to answer a question, it may still try to produce an answer based on what it has learnt. This is one reason

hallucinations

 can happen.


Multimodality


Pre-trained knowledge is still mainly about patterns learnt from text and other training data …

author: JournalAvant
title: In What Ways Does Capitalism Dominate? - Emma Gustavsson
content:
Editor’s Note: The author of this piece is an independent researcher and philosophy student in Stockholm, Sweden. She serves on the editorial board of Tidskriften Ordning, and works at the intersection of value-form theory, critical theory, and the history of political thought. Her personal website is www.Kommunismen.org.

A PDF of this piece can be found at the bottom of the page.

There is a conversation I seem unable to avoid. It returns at my parents’ kitchen table and in the late hours when my partner and I cannot sleep. At some point I say that it does not finally matter which of the parties forms the next government, because the social order that follows the election will be recognizably the order that preceded it. The reply is always quick and a little wounded. My partner, who disagrees with me about most things political, says that if the parties are interchangeable then politics is a fiction, and that I have talked myself into a position from which nothing can be done.

I do not think they are mistaken about what they defend. The differences between governments are real, and they are felt in places where abstraction has no purchase: in a clinic or a deportation order, in the difference between a rent that can be paid and one that cannot. To say that these differences do not matter would be both false and cruel. But this was never my claim. What I have been trying to say is that beneath the visible contest of programs there is a level of social life that no program reaches, and that this level persists, intact, through every alternation of the parties that manage it.

This article is not, in the first instance, an argument for revolution. Neither is it a critique of electoral politics as such. I have no wish to tell my friend that his evenings of canvassing were wasted, or to confirm my partner’s suspicion that I have reasoned my way into paralysis. The question I want to pursue lies between reform and rupture. If a given social order reasserts itself regardless of who administers it, then the interesting question is not whom we should elect but what kind of order possesses this strange capacity to survive its own elections. What are the structures that make such persistence possible? Why is capitalist society so difficult to govern out of existence, even by those who sincerely wish to? These are questions about domination, and they are the questions of this article.

To pose them properly, one has to set aside a familiar picture. In ordinary speech, and in much of the press, capitalism names a set of policies or a cluster of institutions: private property, the joint-stock company, the firm, and the market understood as a place where things are bought and sold. In this reformist picture, to change capitalism would be to change the policies and reform the institutions, and the reason this proves so hard is simply that powerful people resist it. There is truth in this, but it remains on the surface. It mistakes the symptoms of a relation for the relation itself. Capitalism, in the sense I mean to develop here, is not primarily an institution or a body of law. It is a social relation, and more precisely a relation governed by the self-valorization of value, by the compulsion that money be advanced in order to return as more money. Value that valorizes itself [sich verwertender Wert] is the master of this society in a sense that no minister can be, though this mastery is the form of an inversion [Verkehrung] and not the rule of a subject standing behind the process. Institutions and laws are the forms this relation assumes and the channels through which it moves, but they are not its basis. One can rearrange them considerably and leave the relation untouched, which is precisely what the alternation of governments tends to do.

This is why Marx insisted that what has to be explained about such a society is not only how it produces things but how it reproduces itself. A society does not persist by accident. The worker who sells her labor in order to live, and who in living renews the need to sell it tomorrow, reproduces in the same motion the relation that compels the sale. Capital, for Marx, presupposes the conditions of its own existence and reposits them through its own movement, so that the result of the process is the restoration of its premise. As Søren Mau puts it in Mute Compulsion “capital presupposes its own presuppositions”. A social order with this character is not held in place by a single …

author: Pip Hinman
title: Ecosocialism 2026 forges unity and builds struggles
content:
“The big people behind capitalism are quite aware that they are planning the end of the world as we know it”, Sabrina Fernandes, a political economist and ecosocialist activist from Brazil, told the Ecosocialism 2026 conference in Magan-djin/Brisbane, September 11–13.

“They don’t have a problem with the world ending as we know it — as long as they can keep making profits,” Fernandes said.

“They do have a problem with a society that they might not be able to control when things get really hard, as we are coming to this stage of ecocide and global catastrophe. They are fighting over the spoils of war and climate change.”

Places that would not normally be considered part of the grab are becoming so, Fernandes said. The oceans “are a new terra nullius for them” — for ocean floor mining.

There should be an international agreement for this, but US President Donald Trump does not care and has begun issuing his own licences, she added.

Helen Yaffe, author, activist and Professor of Latin American Political Economy, University of Glasgow, told the conference that socialist Cuba, one of the key targets of Trump’s new colonialism, is facing multiple and mounting challenges as the US blockade intensifies.

The response that she has witnessed, in a recent visit to Cuba, was: “We shall not submit!”

“Revolutionary Cuba wrote the rulebook on resilience,” Yaffe said. Facing a total oil blockade since January, Cuba is now undertaking an incredibly rapid transition to renewable energies.

“Many commentators are saying this will be the fastest ever transition.” Solar panel parks now supply more than 60% of electricity on some days, but Yaffe said the challenge is storage.

Singaporean ecosocialist See Yong Feng, another guest speaker, told Green Left that capitalism is holding back human development.

“The need for limitless economic growth is often framed as the only way to solve global poverty, but new research strongly disproves this. The world already uses way more than enough energy and materials to provide a decent standard of living for all, but the profit-driven capitalist system prevents this from happening.

“We can both address poverty and the climate crisis, as long as we break the capitalist elites’ control of our economy and democratise our production and consumption,” See said.

The Gaza genocide, Trump’s blatant disregard for international and domestic laws and his naked colonial violence symbolise the ugly reality that is forging a new generation of activists, Alex Bainbridge, a conference organiser, told GL.

“Trump has his admirers and imitators all around the world, including Marine Le Pen in France, Narendra Modi in India and Pauline Hanson here.

“But while far-right politicians push hard, there is a sharp reaction and a growing resistance; this conference was a powerful reminder of that,” Bainbridge said.

Remah Naji, a leading activist with Justice for Palestine Magan-djin, expressed this resistance. “Maybe we can’t stop a fascist and psychopath like Netanyahu from committing the war crimes he’s committing … but I can hold my government to account.”

The conference included a solidarity concert with Phil Monsour and an art exhibition.

Markela Panegyres, another conference organiser and curator of the art exhibition, told GL: “From the ongoing genocide in Gaza, to the endless drive to more wars and militarism, to ecocide, to the rise of the far right, the depravity of US-led imperialism and global capitalism is reaching ever-higher levels.

“The gravity of this moment demands that art and artists play an active role in resistance.

“This is why the concept of cultural intifada is so important: Art should not be merely a reflection of life, or entertainment or a commodity, but a weapon in the struggle for our collective liberation.

“The work of the artists, musicians and theatre makers who participated in the cultural intifada round-table and exhibition demonstrated the importance of art in movement-building.

“We were so proud that Aunty Sue Coleman-Haseldine, a senior Googatha Elder, Maralinga survivor and long-term anti-nuclear activist, came all the way from the Googatha Nation in the west of South Australia, north of Ceduna.”

Coleman-Haseldine talked about the campaign against rocket and weapons testing on her Country and her opposition to AUKUS and to US military and surveillance bases.

Ecosocialism 2026 was sponsored by the Socialist Alliance, Green Left, Resistance Books and Links — International …

author: Julius Gavroche
title: Against the Tide
content:
from

New Left Review-Sidecar

,

18/09/2026


by Morten Høi Jensen


Prospective biographers of Victor Serge begin at a disadvantage. 

Memoirs of a Revolutionary

 (1951) is one of the great autobiographies of the last century, vividly recounting the twists and turns – from Belgium to France, Spain, Russia, Mexico – of a spectacularly dramatic political life. Yet as Mitchell Abidor argues in his recent biography, Serge’s story ‘is more complex than his memoirs would lead the reader to believe’. 

Victor Serge: Unruly Revolutionary

 aims to ‘roughen edges’ that the memoirist smoothed over and probe ‘contradictions’ that he minimized. Begun as an attempt to help Richard Greeman complete his own, never completed biography of Serge, Abidor’s account draws on the astonishing archive of material Greeman spent a lifetime assembling. While Suzi Weissman’s impassioned 

Victor Serge: A Political Biography

 (2001) was written to rescue Serge’s legacy from post-Cold War triumphalism, Abidor offers a cooler and more sceptical account, leaving no ideological inconsistency unexamined.


Though admiring of his subject, Abidor is keen to dispel the mythology around ‘Saint Serge’. He begins by deflating the family lore with which 

Memoirs of a Revolutionary

 opens: that Serge – born Victor Kibalchich in Brussels in 1890 – was distantly related to a Russian revolutionary and bomb maker executed in 1881 for his role in the assassination of Tsar Alexander II. Abidor explains that no genealogical evidence has been found. In his view, ‘Serge’s connection was, instead, an emotional one, a political and moral one, and so became a real one psychologically.’ The idea that he grew up among Russian revolutionary exiles is also a ‘good deal less straightforward’ than he would later suggest. Abidor documents the difficulties of Serge’s early life. His father, Léon, had been expelled from the military academy in St Petersburg for possessing revolutionary propaganda, then fled to Switzerland, where he met Serge’s mother, Vera. They lived a peripatetic and straitened existence, moving between ‘the slums of Brussels, Canterbury, Geneva and London’, before splitting up. Serge ‘was born into a shabby broken home, one he left when he was only a child’. Family mythology it seems, filled a void – and in later years, served as solace in times of great adversity.


Living on his own from the age of twelve and lacking a formal education, Serge immersed himself in Brussels’ left-wing milieu, reading Kropotkin as well as Louis Blanc’s 

History of the French Revolution

, joining the youth branch of the Belgian Workers’ Party and starting a newspaper, 

Le Communiste

, with a group of friends. Yet they soon found this ‘solidly reformist social-democratic’ formation constricting, and left it in 1907, storming out of a party congress after leader Emil Vandervelde called for support for the annexation of Congo. 

Le Communiste

 was renamed 

Le Révolté.

 Writing under the name Le Rétif – ‘an adjective with many meanings: restive, recalcitrant, refractory, rebel, stubborn, unruly’, Abidor writes – Serge espoused an individualist strain of anarchism that combined disdain for the masses with a quasi-Nietzschean veneration of the individual’s capacity for revolt, in the service of which crime and terror were admissible tactics.


After 

Le Révolté

 defended the anarchist bomb maker Abraham Hartenstein, who in February 1909 shot and killed two police officers, Serge found it impossible to continue living in Brussels. That summer, he decamped for Paris, home of ‘anarchy, literature and revolution’. Abidor points to some retrospective modification – ‘a professional deformation of all memoirists’ – in Serge’s description of what drew him there, and what the city represented. As a young anarchist he ‘would not have seen Paris as the city of the Commune, which he mocked in several articles, or the syndicalist CGT, which he would also condemn, and certainly not Lenin, whom he would have been less familiar with than the Bolshevik’s Narodnik brother, the martyred Alexander’, Abidor writes. Serge established himself as a prominent anarchist thinker, writing for the movement’s central newspaper, 

l’anarchie

, under various pseudonyms. He continued to offer vocal support to those he saw as rebelling against the state. ‘The right to live implies the right to kill whoever prevents me from living’, Serge argued at the time. ‘The will to live imposes on me the duty …

content:
Минюст РФ подкинул сегодня абсурда. В обновленную версию реестра «иноагентов» включен некий Проект «Анархист-35». Мы, Автономное действие, о таком слыхом не слыхивали. В реестре указаны связанные с проектом YouTube канал и страница в соцсети X. Там немного как постов, так и подписчиков. И, главное, к анархизму они практически не имеют отношения.

Это контент правого видеоблогера Вячеслава Мальцева. Бывший вице-спикер Саратовской областной думы, Мальцев стал популярным видеоблогером в середине 2010-х. Он утверждал, что 5 ноября 2017 года в России обязательно случится революция.

Никакой революции в этот день, к сожалению или к счастью, не случилось, но против ряда сторонников Мальцева в 2017 году завели уголовные дела, а сам Вячеслав успел скрыться в Европе. Аресты по делу «Сети» начались в конце 2017 года, поэтому поначалу возникла ложная информация, что в Пензе тоже задерживают сторонников Мальцева.

Единственным лицом, аффилированным с Проектом «Анархист-35», Минюст признал… Мальцева Вячеслава Вячеславовича. Хотя очевидно, что эти страницы в соцсети X и на YouTube создавал не он. content:
La Librairie Publico reçoit Maurice Schuhmann pour une conférence multimédia, fondée sur des revues, des bandes dessinées et des chansons dans laquelle il retrace les débuts de l'après-1945, analyse la négation idéologique de l'anarchisme – ainsi que, dans certains cas, la récupération de penseurs anarchistes par le parti d'État au pouvoir, le

SED

 – et évoque la coopération entre la scène anarchiste et l'Église protestante.


De la zone d'occupation soviétique (

SBZ

) à la

RDA

 jusqu'à la réunification


Après la Seconde Guerre mondiale, le mouvement anarchiste en Allemagne était pratiquement anéanti. Il fallut de nombreuses années avant que de nouvelles initiatives permettent à une scène anarchiste de se reconstituer en République fédérale d'Allemagne. La situation était encore plus difficile pour les militant·es anarchistes de la

RDA

, qui étaient confronté·es à des préjugés idéologiques plus marqués et à une répression étatique plus forte qu'à l'Ouest.


Malgré cela, les anarchistes jouèrent un rôle important au sein de l'opposition de gauche en

RDA

 et contribuèrent finalement à la chute du régime. Leur objectif n'était généralement pas la réunification avec la République fédérale capitaliste, mais la construction d'une société fondée sur le socialisme libertaire.


Cette aspiration s'illustra notamment par la proclamation de la «

 

République d'Utopia

 

» dans la nuit précédant la réunification officielle de l'Allemagne.

title: OCD Rebellion - Towards an Anarchist centred critical theory of OCD
content:
Author

: OCD Rebellion

Title

: Towards an Anarchist centred critical theory of OCD

Date

: 16/09/26

Source

: Original draft here:

<medium.com/@davidayokadeniyi/towards-an-anarchist-phenomenology-and-critical-theory-of-ocd-b0c36b7744a3>


Looking on the anarchist library there is nothing specifically related to OCD. Ugh.... Same as a few years ago, while there is a lot of criticism of psychiatry and diagnostic logics used to pathologise and often otherise and exclude folks, what is not talked about in detail is specifically OCD, which stands for Obsessive Compulsive Disorder and how it relates to the anti authoritarian and no hierarchical ideology, milieu and ‘state’ of social formation called anarchism, anarchists and an-arche. In terms of. General academic theory there has been an attempt by writers Matthew Hiller and Eva Stepney called “The Paradox of Purity” pointing out certain guidelines for what could make a useful approach to critical theory. It touches on themes and thinkers that I also found relevant such as Mary Douglas and her work on purity, pollution, ritual and dirt such as found in the classic text “Purity and Danger,” in 1966. While I fine essay in and of itself what I often think is a missing thread not only in this article but in larger radical (and even “anarchist”) discussions is the usage of anarchist theory and thinkers which can locate key concerns in not only the phenomenology of OCD but in cultural conceptions which can make it a cross match for critical analysis.


OCD is Dis-Order? Anarchy is Order?


 A lot of critical theories as well as more poststructural theories are about challenging binaries and things which structure and control our life whether of normality, rationality of even concepts of order, chaos and control. As stated in the aforementioned article a Critical OCD approach looks to challenge binaries of Order/Chaos, similar binaries that are crucial to contemporary, social and historical conceptions of anarchy. Anarchist parlance has had a long history with playing between anarchism and its association with chaos, violence and disorder. Anselme Bellagarigue has the famous quote “Anarchy

 is

 order, government is civil war,” with the famous anarchist emblem painting the anarchist A over an O to symbolise in avarice to hegemonic notions that anarchy is in line with harmony order. While some anarchists have thought to recuperate anarchism from negative notions of chaos, messiness and disorder some anarchists have embraced it such as Enzo Martucci in an essay titled “In praise of chaos” who gave chaos a new meaning to signify non conformity, flux and freedom.


 Order is a weird term taking on multiple associations, some metaphorical, some societal and some even at the micro and even visual scale. An example of this is the anarchist inspired writer James C Scott and his use of

 the visual

 in Seeing Like a State to elucidate “Visual and aesthetic” order (A supposes characteristic of Authoritarian High Modernism). OCD can be contrasted to order in many ways but in this section it is interesting to look at the often found label “symmetry/Order” OCD with OCD finding heavy cultural concepts with psychotic levels of neatness, harmony and visual unity with “Im so OCD” often referring to a need to have things in just the right order, so precise as to try to reach absolute perfection. As Meaghan Rice of TalkSPace says “Symmetry and Ordering OCD is a subtype of OCD causes a person to focus excessively on how things look or are arranged, balanced, or positioned.”


 This leads to distress if the compulsions or actions to neaten, balance, position or order/perfect things aren’t done “correctly. While this is just one aspect of OCD it is to note that there has been work with OCD in disability studies regarding order. As the writers of The paradox of Purity put it, “cb5 Disability studies scholars have challenged medicalized and individualized accounts of OCD, arguing that the disorder is instead a symptom of modernity, in which individuals over-internalize social imperatives towards order and control (Davis 11; Castel 302; Fleissner 34). To this end, they present OCD as a constructed category that pathologizes thoughts and behavior that are deemed as excessive or unproductive, with treatment acting to discipline non-normative ways of being.” While not cited in the article, this passage is similar to the one found in “The philosophy of Dirt” on page 126 echoing the work of Norbert …

author: Unknown
title: Уэйн Прайс - Революционный анархизм - часть левого движения?
content:
Автор

: Уэйн Прайс

Название

: Революционный анархизм - часть левого движения?

Дата

: 1991

Дополнительная информация

: Перевод М. Шувалова из газеты “Love and Rage” (USA) октябрь 1991 г. КАС-КОНТАКТ № 18 (25) февраль 1993 года


 Признают ли революционные анархисты себя частью левого движения? Ответов на этот вопрос, видимо, будет столько же, сколько существует на свете анархистов. Довольно типичный ответ принадлежит ветерану анархистского движения Сэму Долгоффу: «Вам всегда нужен левый фланг. И в рамках левого фланга вы ищете еще более левую сторону. Но и там вам нужно что-то еще более левое. И вот это-то левое и есть я».


Более ясное определение этому дал П. А. Кропоткин в своей статье «Анархизм» (1910 г.): «Что же касается их экономических воззрений, то анархисты наряду со всеми социалистами, левое крыло которых они составляют, противостоят… капиталистическому производству» (сокращенная цитата).


Анархизм – левый фланг левых, левое крыло социалистов? Многие хорошие анархисты, я уверен, будут выступать против такого определения. Левые, подчеркивают они, не хотят того, чего мы хотим. Левые, по их мысли, авторитарны, государственники, прокапиталисты, расисты и сексисты… В этом, конечно, есть доля правды, но тем не менее…


Вообще, организованное левое движение делится на два основных течения: реформистское и революционное. Левые реформисты варьируется от откровенных прокапиталистических либералов из числа социал-демократов (или «демократических социалистов») до умеренных коммунистов. Все они хотят использовать существующую бюрократически-милитаристскую машину государства для проведения социальных изменений, в общем принимая капиталистическую экономику, но стремясь ослабить ее наиболее негативные черты при помощи государственного регулирования и государственной собственности на некоторые виды производства. Реформисты считают, что нет альтернативы нынешней системе, которая угрожает всему человечеству своими войнами и угрозой экологической катастрофы. Вообще же, хотя реформисты заявляют, что они последовательно ведут людей к построению социалистического общества, но тем не менее не существует ни одной крупной социал-демократической партии, которая уже успела это сделать. Современные европейские социал-демократы (и даже очень многие коммунисты) очень мало чем отличаются от либеральных демократов традиционного образца…


С другой стороны, революционные левые нацеливают свою деятельность на уничтожение существующего государства. Но большинство из них (марксисты-ленинцы или националисты) хотели бы заменить его новым государством – государством однопартийной диктатуры… Они считают, что это будет вполне приемлемая «бархатная» диктатура – «диктатура пролетариата», или что-нибудь еще в этом роде.


В сущности, они стремятся отобрать все богатства и достояние у нынешних капиталистов, национализировав всю экономику. Они называют это «социализмом», но на самом деле это государственный капитализм. При таком порядке бюрократия очень быстро станет новым капиталистическим классом и неизбежно введет жесткий тоталитаризм…


В настоящее время марксизм-ленинизм дискредитирован как никогда ранее, а социал-демократия мертва как идея, хотя и продолжают существовать европейские партии, называющие себя «социал-демократами», поэтому многие анархисты считают: почему мы должны идентифицировать анархизм с прогнившим на корню левым движением? Зачем держаться за этот скомпрометированный и пользующийся дурной славой ярлык?


ЛЕВЫЕ - ЭТО ОППОЗИЦИЯ


 В этих аргументах много верного. Мы согласны с основной позицией, что необходимо провести четкую границу между анархизмом и либерализмом (или государственным социализмом). И в то же время я считаю, что успех анархического движения будет основываться на нашем умении быть самыми левыми из левых.


Левые – это прежде всего оппозиция. Если рассматривать левое движение в более общем смысле, не придавая значения партиям и программам, то можно сказать, что левые – это прежде всего объединение людей, которые выступают против эксплуатации трудящихся, угнетения женщин, негров, «голубых» и других групп населения, против империалистических войн, против разрушения окружающей среды – одним словом, против всех зол, за которые ответственно нынешнее общество.


Профсоюзные активисты, феминистки, борцы с расизмом и дискриминацией гомосексуалистов, экологисты и т. д., и т. п. – все это «левые» в широком смысле слова. В некоторых странах они предпочитают называть себя «либералами» или «прогрессивистами». В других же …

author: ROAPE
title: Food security or seed capture? The colonial potato and Africa’s seed wars
content:
It all begins with a potato. Not the kind that nourishes a nation in textbook stories, but a colonial potato. This potato was shipped, tested, rationed, pushed through mission gardens and military supply lines, and ultimately sold as progress. Tracing that potato across Nigeria’s highlands leads to today’s disputes over seed, debt, law, and who decides what African farmers cultivate. 


Seeds are not just seeds. They carry memory, labour, taste, law, power, and often, debt.

The colonial potato scheme in Nigeria

 is significant because it shows how dependency on seeds can develop even before it is codified in law. Nowadays, discussions about seed sovereignty in Africa often centre on patents, plant breeders’ rights, certified seed laws, and agribusiness. However, colonial Nigeria reveals an older method of control: emergency.       


In the 1930s and 1940s, British officials transformed the

Jos and Mambila Plateaus

 into experimental sites for growing potatos. Initially, the scheme was small and awkward, driven by European miners, missionaries, and colonial officers seeking familiar food. Then, the Second World War (1939-1945) changed everything. Supply routes were disrupted, troops needed food, and Nigerian highland farmers were forcibly integrated into a larger imperial food plan. An agricultural experiment became part of the British empire’s war effort.


An anthropological base map of Plateau Province reproduced from C.G. Ames, The Gazetteers of Plateau Province, 1932 (Copy in Nigerian National Archives, Kaduna)


The highlands were ideal for the crop. Potatos thrive in cooler conditions, and Jos and Mambila provided the climate colonial agronomists desired. However, these areas were not empty spaces waiting for improvement. They were inhabited, farmed, and politically complex societies with their own crops, markets, and knowledge systems.


Colonial rule altered the dynamics in these regions. Tin mining on the Jos Plateau attracted workers, administrators, and settlers. Demand for European foods increased. Potatos, once a garden crop for expatriates and mission stations, began to seem valuable to the colonial state.


Starting in the 1930s, British

officials based in Nigeria began importing seed potatos from Ireland, Britain, Europe, South Africa, the Canary Islands, and the United States.

 Mission stations cultivated the potatos. District heads distributed the seed. Farmers cautiously tried the crop, incorporating it into local routines where it made sense while rejecting it when it didn’t. The potato became a means of power.


This did not mean that older crops and seed systems disappeared. There was no formal ban, and local farmers continued to grow, save, and exchange seed in various ways. The scheme worked in subtler ways: it altered the rewards. Access to land, labour, credit, official support, and markets began to favour the colonial crop. Imported seed was seen as improved, while farmer-saved seed and local knowledge were pushed to the sidelines. Over time, diverse and adaptable seed systems were narrowed, though not completely erased, by a supply chain prioritising mines, mission stations, military demands, and imperial markets.


Before the Second World War, the scheme was no great success. Some farmers thought potatos were poisonous. Others saw no reason to cultivate a crop with a limited, European-dominated market. A 1937 attempt to sell imported ‘Great Scott’ seed potatos to the Jos Native Authority ended poorly: half went unsold, the remainder was given away, and the scheme lost money.


War transformed failure into urgency. The empire needed food close to military outposts. It aimed to save cargo space and lessen reliance on disrupted shipping routes. Suddenly, potatos on the Mambila and Jos Plateau became crucial.


The war economy and the creation of dependency


Production surged from around

90 tons at the beginning of the war in 1939 to about 1,200 tons by 1943. Seed stores and experimental stations emerged throughout Kagoro, Zonkwa, Kurmin Biri, and Riyom

. Colonial science advanced rapidly, too: London-based Kew scientists devised ways to transport sprouting ‘eyes’ of potatos instead of whole tubers, facilitating a steady supply from outside.


Wartime officials did not establish an independent Nigerian seed system; they created a supply chain. Farmers were encouraged to boost production. Yet, this authority remained elsewhere: seed, disease control, imports, and markets remained …

title: “Logic of Elimination” Drives Israel’s Policies in the West Bank, Report Finds
content:
The report says Israel is “dramatically intensifying its attacks on every aspect of Palestinian life in the West Bank.”

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

A major new report by the Israeli human rights group B’Tselem titled “The Elimination Project” accuses Israel of “dramatically intensifying its attacks on every aspect of Palestinian life in the West Bank.”

“For too long, Israel’s policies in the West Bank have been treated or looked at as isolated events,” says Ori Givati, director of international relations at B’Tselem. “We actually find that there is one very coherent logic behind all of them, and this is the logic of elimination of Palestinian collective life in the West Bank.” Givati says tactics against Palestinians intensified with Israel’s 2022 election and again after October 7, 2023, adding that “we are definitely seeing a lot of the mechanisms, the tools that were used and are used still … in Gaza, being implemented in the West Bank.”

We also speak with Mohammad Sha’ban, a Palestinian farmer from Halhul in the Hebron area of the occupied West Bank who says 11 gates and seven settler outposts have been installed around Halhul since 2025. “We cannot reach our lands. We cannot go outside Halhul. They open only one gate from 8 o’clock until 5 o’clock every day,” says Sha’ban. Settlers “attack farmers, beat farmers … damaging our cars, also damaging our fields, uprooting our trees.”

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

Our new report “The Elimination Project” shows how this mechanism works and how over the past three years, it has become more lethal, violent and explicit. The Elimination Project in the West Bank operates through five domains of action that work together and reinforce each other: killing, violence, intimidation, movement restrictions, economic strangulation, social and political destruction, ethnic cleansing and territorial takeover. author: Unknown
title: The International Dimension of “Arab Authoritarianism”
content:
Title

: The International Dimension of “Arab Authoritarianism”

Date

: 29 April 2026

Source

: “The I.B. Tauris Handbook of Authoritarianism in the Arab World”, 2026


Introduction


 Authoritarian power in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) is predominantly understood as pertaining to authoritarian regimes and to the open repression and violence deployed by Arab dictators, unelected monarchs, secret service agencies, the police, and militaries. While those actors are without doubt key pillars for the maintenance and deepening of authoritarian power, an exclusive focus on regime actors ignores the fact that the (Arab) state has become a globalized institution.

[1]

 As the transnational and/or international dimension of authoritarian power is downplayed and/or ignored, Orientalist discourses and deeply problematic binaries of Western democracies vs. Arab autocracies are perpetuated. Drawing on the emerging body of literature that explores this international dimension of authoritarian power,

[2]

 this chapter seeks to discuss select examples that illustrate the ways in which authoritarian power structures in the MENA, despite their violent local manifestations, are inherently transregional and global.


 Emphasizing the “dynamic nature of governance,” Glasius focuses on “extraterritorial practices” and the territorial unboundedness of authoritarian power.

[3]

 Bruff and Tansel, Hanieh, and others have shown the close interconnection between global processes of capital accumulation and authoritarian power.

[4]

 The financialization and commodification of nature at large and of renewable energies in particular further resource extraction and exploitative labor regimes. Public-private partnerships increase public debt and reproduce socioeconomic inequalities. EU and US efforts at externalizing the authoritarian effects of violent and repressive migration regimes also point to transregional connections. Further, El Kurd has illustrated through the example of efforts at Arab-Israeli normalization how peace initiatives may facilitate authoritarian practices.

[5]

 Finally, El Kurd, Brownlee, and Schuetze have demonstrated how processes of technocratization—often directly supported by so-called “development agencies” and/or “democracy promoters”—enable the reproduction of authoritarian power behind a façade of seemingly ongoing procedural reforms.

[6]


 If these global connections of “Arab authoritarianism” remain unexposed, our understanding and analysis of “Arab authoritarianism” remain incomplete, and its violent and repressive manifestations become harder to contest. By focusing on authoritarian practices and their spatial and temporal articulations,

[7]

 and by demonstrating the fundamental mismatch between the involved actors on the one side and the territorial boundaries implicit to notions of “Arab authoritarianism” on the other, this chapter argues that more attention must be paid to the inherently international dimension of “Arab authoritarianism.” The chapter illustrates this by exploring how debt-funding of renewable energy megaprojects in Morocco, EU-Tunisian collaboration in the fight against migration, “Western”-supported efforts at Arab-Israeli normalization in Jordan, and US and European “democracy promotion” initiatives must all be understood as inherent components of “Arab Authoritarianism.” While the selected examples do not cover all aspects of the international dimension of “Arab authoritarianism,” they focus on key dynamics shaping regional politics: neoliberal continuities in efforts at transitioning to post-fossil politics, structural racism and the violent containment of migration, Israeli settler colonialism and its role within US imperialism, and liberalism’s unabated claims to moral superiority, which effectively only serve to further reinforce the mentioned forms of structural violence.


Climate Crisis, Neoliberalism, and the Debt Financing of RE Megaprojects


 The intersection of the climate crisis and authoritarian practices in the MENA region requires more than an analysis of environmental policies; it calls for a critical examination of the neoliberal economic structures that sustain them. The urgency to transition away from fossil fuels and secure energy independence has sparked an unprecedented push for ambitious renewable energy (RE) plans in North African countries.

[8]

author: David Swanson
title: Abolish the Board of Peace. Try the Table of Peace.
content:
Nonviolent Activism, North America, What to do

By David Swanson, World BEYOND War, September 5, 2026

I don’t mean to complain about the Board of Peace. If you want to ensure endless wars, expand settler colonialism, formally empower oligarchs over nations, destroy the United Nations, and keep genocides rolling along, I’m sure it’s fantastic!

But I recommend, at least in addition, trying the table of peace. This is something I tried in Charlottesville, Virginia, on Saturday. First, you’ll need a table. Then you’ll need some supplies. I recommend free stickers, bookmarks, and flyers, some books, some sign up sheets, some display boards, a jar for donations, a banner. Bring all this stuff and a few friendly people to a farmer’s market.

And you’ll need one more thing: a game. Here’s how I did that. I asked people to pretend to be the United States Congress for 10 seconds. (Many of them were disgusted at the thought but I assured them they could shower afterwards.) Then I gave them 12 stones and told them it was the federal discretionary budget for 2027. I asked them to distribute the stones in eight glasses labeled: Environmental Protection; Education; Labor, Small Business Administration, and Commerce; Health and Human Services; Housing and Urban Development, Interior, and Transportation; War and war preparations; Energy; and Other. If they asked “Now is this green energy or fossil fuel energy?” or “Is this education as it should be done or the dy$#@! they do now?” then I told them it was their ideal form of energy or education.

A lot of people played the game.

Environmental Protection won. Very close behind that were Education and Health and Human Services. Not far behind those was Energy, which everyone told me was renewable energy. Housing and Labor came next. And one gentleman the entire time I was tabling put one stone into War. He explained, almost apologetically, that it was for the “defensive wars.” I backed away slowly and kept my eyes on him.

When each person had finished distributing the stones, I showed them a pie chart illustrating the budget proposed for 2027 by Trump. The glass that people had left almost empty eats up 77.66% of the pie. The categories people wanted funded most get the tiniest slivers.

Not everybody will play the game. Some people will take a sticker and keep walking without slowing down. Some people will stop and talk. Others will buy a book, sign a pledge, etc. With the ones who will devote 60 seconds or more, your goal is of course to get them engaged. Will they sign up and get involved? Will they take some flyers to distribute? Here, I think, it’s important to understand that success is measured in very small numbers. If you can get a few people doing more than they were before, that’s a win.

Many people, those who don’t slow down and those who stop to chat, will assure you that all is fine because they plan to vote in an election. I live in a district and state and nation with no anti-war candidates running for any offices, but even if that were not the case, the delusion that voting fixes everything and that no one can do anything other than voting would still be by far the single biggest hurdle to effective participation in society.

Many will tell you how deeply they agree regarding war and peace, and how sorry they are that all is hopeless and doomed by “human nature,” or “sociopaths,” or “money” — they’ve got a million of these. Others will thank you for what you’re doing — conveying the meaning that they’re glad you’re doing it so that they don’t have to.

But there’s usually a few percent who will actually get active and educate and agitate and demonstrate. Get them, and you’ll have done your part toward finding that few percent of the whole population that is needed to change the world.

content:
Le groupe local de Paris de l'

Agent Orange, une bombe à retardement

.


Le groupe local Paris Nord Est de l'Union Communiste Libertaire vous invite à une projection-débat autour du film

Agent Orange, une bombe à retardement

, de Thuy Tien Ho et Laurent Lindebrings.


En quittant le Vietnam en 1975, l'armée américaine a laissé un poison invisible : la dioxine. Cette arme chimique puissante, plus connue sous le nom d'Agent Orange, produite par la multinationale Monsanto, a pris possession de la terre, des eaux, de la végétation. En s'infiltrant dans les sols, les rivières, elle touche la chaine alimentaire. Des millions de Vietnamiens sont victimes de la dioxine, atteints de malformations et de cancers. 40 ans après les derniers épandages, la dioxine continue ses ravages. C'est cette utilisation massive de produit toxique qui a conduit à théoriser la notion d'écocide.


Alors qu'une manifestation se prépare le 3 octobre pour protester contre les pesticides, cette projection et la discussion qui suivra seront l'occasion de se rappeler de l'utilisation des pesticides comme arme de guerre, de soulever l'importance de lutter contre le colonialisme chimique et pour une écologie anti-impérialiste.

EDMP
